meta.title: Python Programming Foundations
meta.topic: Python programming for a complete beginner
meta.summary: A practical six-week path from Python syntax to a small automation project.

brief.goal: Write small, useful Python programs and become ready for a project-focused intermediate course.
brief.background: No Python experience and only limited prior programming exposure.
constraints: Keep the core set to three resources
assumptions: The learner can install Python or use a browser-based environment
The learner wants general automation rather than data science specialization

guide.bottom_line: Start with the official Python runtime and a plain code editor, learn only the syntax needed to automate one real file or text task, and use short exercises for feedback. Do not begin with frameworks, data-science stacks, or a long survey course.
key_points: Typing and modifying working examples builds useful fluency faster than passive watching.
Functions, collections, files, and error handling cover most beginner automation tasks.
One small end-to-end script is a better six-week checkpoint than broad but shallow topic coverage.

recommendations.choice: Official tutorial plus a local Python installation
recommendations.best_for: Learning canonical behavior and becoming comfortable running real files
recommendations.why: It keeps the environment close to how Python is actually used and provides authoritative syntax explanations.
recommendations.tradeoffs: The tutorial assumes some general programming familiarity, so a complete beginner needs a gentler project resource alongside it.

recommendations.choice: Automate the Boring Stuff as the project spine
recommendations.best_for: A complete beginner motivated by useful office or file automation
recommendations.why: Its examples turn syntax into recognizable tasks instead of treating Python as abstract theory.
recommendations.tradeoffs: The book is much broader than this plan; only the assigned chapters and one project should be core.

sections.title: Use one simple toolchain
sections.purpose: Choose where to run, write, and practice Python without wasting the first week on tooling.

items.name: Runtime
items.explanation: Install the current stable Python 3 release and run files locally. Use a browser notebook only when installation is blocked.
examples: Google Colab as a temporary fallback

items.name: Editor
items.explanation: Use one editor with syntax highlighting and a visible terminal for the full six-week path.
examples: Visual Studio Code with the Microsoft Python extension

items.name: Practice loop
items.explanation: End every session with code that runs or a documented error you can explain; passive watching does not count as practice.

sections.title: Learn capabilities in dependency order
sections.purpose: Focus on the smallest concept sequence that leads to a useful automation script.

items.name: Run and read code
items.explanation: Start with expressions, variables, strings, input, output, and reading simple tracebacks.

items.name: Control and reuse
items.explanation: Add conditions, loops, and functions so a script can make decisions and avoid repeated code.

items.name: Process data and files
items.explanation: Use lists, dictionaries, text processing, and files to solve realistic automation tasks.

items.name: Make the script reliable
items.explanation: Handle empty and invalid inputs, break work into functions, and document how another person can run the program.

next_action.action: Open The Python Tutorial and run the examples in sections 1–3, changing at least one value in every example.
next_action.output: A saved Python file containing three modified examples and one sentence about what each demonstrates.

resource_tracks.title: Short-session practical track
resource_tracks.best_for: A beginner learning in 30–45 minute sessions who wants visible progress every day
sequence: Read one assigned Automate the Boring Stuff section for no more than 15 minutes.
Type and alter the example for 15 minutes.
Use the remaining time for one small Exercism task or one debugging note.
Consult the matching Python Tutorial section only when a concept needs a canonical explanation.

resource_tracks.title: Reference-first track
resource_tracks.best_for: A learner who prefers precise written explanations and can sustain 60–90 minute sessions
sequence: Study the assigned Python Tutorial section and run every example.
Finish one or two concept exercises and record any errors that required documentation.

resources.title: The Python Tutorial
resources.creator: Python Software Foundation
resources.level: Beginner with some general programming familiarity
resources.best_for: Learners who want precise, canonical explanations and do not mind dense reading
resources.access: Free web access; no account required
resources.why: It is the canonical introduction to Python language concepts and current standard behavior.
resources.focus: Sections 1–8 first; use later sections as references when the roadmap calls for them.
resources.limitations: It explicitly expects basic programming understanding and is less project-driven than a beginner course.

resources.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
resources.creator: Al Sweigart
resources.time: 14–18 hours for selected chapters and one project
resources.best_for: Complete beginners motivated by short, useful automation projects
resources.access: Free to read on the web; optional paid editions and courses
resources.why: It connects fundamentals to concrete automation tasks and is available to read online.
resources.focus: Chapters 1–12, then choose one automation chapter that matches the learner’s interests.
resources.limitations: The project breadth is wider than this six-week path, so most later chapters should be treated as optional.

resources.title: Python on Exercism
resources.creator: Exercism
resources.format: Coding exercises, automated analysis, and mentoring
resources.best_for: Short practice sessions with immediate automated feedback
resources.why: It provides deliberate practice and fast feedback that complements reading and projects.
resources.focus: Complete the tutorial exercise and selected concept exercises on basics, conditions, loops, strings, lists, and dictionaries.
resources.limitations: The catalog and mentoring availability can change, and an account may be needed for the full workflow.

roadmap.title: Learn to read and run Python
objectives: Use values, variables, strings, conditions, loops, and functions
Explain a traceback at a basic level
tasks: Complete Automate the Boring Stuff chapters 1–5
Rewrite five examples from memory and deliberately trigger three errors
roadmap.deliverable: A command-line number or text game using at least one function and one loop.
completion_criteria: Explain variables, conditions, loops, functions, and exceptions without notes
Fix a syntax error and a simple runtime error
Run the deliverable from a clean terminal session
optional: Add input validation to the game

roadmap.title: Work with data and files
objectives: Break a problem into small functions
tasks: Complete Automate the Boring Stuff chapters 6–10
Solve six selected Exercism concept exercises
Write a script that reads a text file and produces a summary
roadmap.deliverable: A tested text-processing utility with a short usage guide.
completion_criteria: Choose an appropriate list or dictionary for a new problem
Read and write a UTF-8 text file safely
Explain the program’s function boundaries and error handling

roadmap.title: Build a useful automation project
objectives: Test and explain an end-to-end script
tasks: Choose one automation problem involving files, text, or structured data
Write a one-page plan before coding
Implement the project in small functions
Test normal, empty, and invalid inputs
roadmap.deliverable: A reusable automation script, tests or a verification checklist, and a one-page project note.
completion_criteria: A new user can run the script from the usage instructions
The script handles at least two failure cases
The learner can explain every function and identify the next improvement
optional: Package the script as a command-line tool
Request feedback on one Exercism solution

source_directory.selection_note: The core set combines one canonical language source, one beginner project source, and one feedback-oriented practice source. Each resource is free on the web and assigned in exact portions.

groups.name: Official documentation
groups.description: Use for canonical Python behavior, terminology, and version-current explanations.

groups.name: Open book
groups.description: Use for complete-beginner explanations and practical automation projects.

groups.name: Practice platform
groups.description: Use for short exercises, automated feedback, and optional mentoring.
